candidates.why: At 11733 `o->color.name = o->color.book_name;` makes both fields point to the SAME strdup'd block. At 11739-11742 `tmp = o->color.name` is freed, but `o->color.book_name` is left dangling and still points at that freed block. Any later read of `book_name` (e.g. the LOG_TRACE at 11761, or free.c:197-198 which frees both `color.name` and `color.book_name`) touches freed memory / double-frees.

At 11748 `o->color.name = strdup (x + 1)` where `x` points INTO `o->color.book_name` (from strchr at 11730). Then at 11749 `x[0]='\0'` mutates book_name, and at 11752-11755 book_name is converted and the old buffer freed. The name/book_name pair is derived from one buffer and freed in a different order than it was created; the same tmp/free dance at 11756-11759 is fragile if the two ever alias again.

`dwg_obj_mlinestyle_get_name` returns the field itself for pre-R2007 (line 6936, no copy), while `dwg_obj_mlinestyle_set_name` does `mlinestyle->name = dwg_add_u8_input (dwg, name)` (6961) with no free of the old value. A caller passing the getter result straight back as `name` makes source and destination the same field: the old buffer is leaked and, in the R2007+ path, the getter's fresh bit_convert_TU copy is the only thing keeping the string alive.

Same pattern as name: `dwg_obj_mlinestyle_get_desc` returns `mlinestyle->description` uncopied for pre-R2007 (line 6987), and `dwg_obj_mlinestyle_set_desc` overwrites it at 7012 via dwg_add_u8_input without freeing the previous allocation. Self-assignment through the getter/setter pair aliases source and destination.

`dynapi_set_helper` has the `free (old)` commented out at 14087, then unconditionally overwrites the destination pointer at 14098/14120/14123. Callers such as in_dxf.c:11449 and in_dxf.c:11165 pass a stack `color` whose `.name` was just set by dwg_add_u8_input (11444 / 11151); the previously stored field value is silently dropped. Not a UAF by itself, but the missing free means any caller that still holds the old pointer is reading a buffer that is now unreachable/leaked.
